title: Smart Bin
intro: Build a bin that opens its lid by itself when a hand comes close: no touching!

wiring_steps.title: The distance sensor
wiring_steps.text: Unplug the USB cable before you change any wires. Plug it back in when you're done. Start with the power rails: a black wire from GND on your board to the blue (−) rail at the bottom of the breadboard, and a red wire from {{VCC}} to the red (+) rail. Push the distance sensor's four pins into J20 to J23, facing out from the breadboard. Wire {{pin:TRIG_PIN}} to G21 (Trig) and a black wire from F23 (Gnd) to the blue (−) rail. The sensor needs 5V: on a 5V board a red wire goes from F20 to the red (+) rail, and Echo goes straight to {{pin:ECHO_PIN}} from H22. ⚠ On an ESP board, the red wire goes from F20 to {{5V}}, and Echo's 5V would hurt the pin, so it goes through two 10kΩ resistors that halve it: one from G22 across the gap to E22, one from D22 to D26, a black wire from A26 to the blue (−) rail, and a wire from C22 to {{pin:ECHO_PIN}}.

wiring_steps.title: The lid servo
wiring_steps.text: The servo is the motor that lifts the lid. Plug three wires into its plug. Brown (or black) goes to the blue (−) rail, orange (or yellow) goes to {{pin:SERVO_PIN}}, and red is power. This part needs 5V. On a 5V board (Uno, Nano, Mega) it uses the red (+) rail. On an ESP board the rail is only 3.3V, so its red wire goes straight to {{5V}} on the board.

wiring_steps.title: The LED
wiring_steps.text: The LED shows when the lid is open. Push it into holes H2 and H3, with the long leg (+) in H3. Put a 220Ω resistor from G2 across the gap to E2. Add a wire from {{pin:LED_PIN}} to J3, and a black wire from A2 to the blue (−) rail at the bottom.

steps.title: Move the lid
steps.text:
A servo is a motor that turns to the angle you ask for, from 0° to 180°. On the bin, **0°** lifts the lid open and **90°** puts it down.

`lid.write(0)` opens the lid. **Your task:** fill in the blank so the lid closes again, then press **Run**.
hints: The blank is the angle for closed.

checks.label: I saw the lid open and close

steps.success: Your bin can open and close its lid. Now it needs to know when to do it.

steps.title: Measure the distance
steps.text:
The distance sensor works like a bat: it sends a squeak too high for us to hear, and times how long the echo takes to come back.

The `measureCm()` function does the measuring, and saves the answer in `cm`. **Your task:** fill in the blank so the Serial Monitor shows `cm`, then Run and move your hand towards the sensor. (In the simulator, drag the distance slider.)
hints: You want to print the distance.
The distance is saved in a variable called `cm`.

checks.label: The distance changes when I move my hand

steps.success: Your bin can measure how far away your hand is, with sound!

steps.title: Open for a hand
steps.text:
Now join them up. The bin measures, and **if** a hand is close it opens the lid, waits 5 seconds and closes it.

**Your task:** fill in the blank so the lid opens when a hand is closer than **30 cm**.
hints: How close should a hand be? 30 cm is about a ruler away.

checks.label: It opens for a hand closer than 30 cm
The lid opened when my hand came close

steps.success: A hands-free bin! It decides for itself with **if**.

steps.title: Light while it's open
steps.text:
**Goal:** the LED lights up while the lid is open, and goes off when it closes.

The LED's pin is already set up in `setup()`. Use `digitalWrite` where the comments are.
hints: Put the HIGH line before the lid opens, and a LOW line after it closes.

checks.label: I saw the LED light up while the lid was open

steps.success: Your smart bin opens for a hand and shows when it's open. Well done!

outro: You built a hands-free bin: a **distance sensor** to notice a hand, an **if** to decide, and a **servo** to lift the lid.
stretch: Make the lid stay open while the hand is still there, and close 5 seconds after it goes.
Change the LED to blink while the lid is moving.
Add a buzzer that beeps when the lid opens.
